name: Wired from Birth: The BCI Transition, 2091-2160
description: An early and largely uncritical history of BCI development and mass adoption, tracing the technology from military neural interface prototypes through the consumer BCI rollout programs of the 2120s-2150s. Produced during a period before BCI criticism became politically organized, the documentary has an unintentional candor about the coercive aspects of early adoption — framing them positively — that later viewers found damning. It is now used by both BCI advocates and refuser movements as evidence, for opposite reasons.
cultural_impact: The documentary's inadvertently honest framing of early BCI coercion became a primary reference text for the consent rights movement of the 2210s, despite having been made as promotional material.
story_hooks: A researcher finds a segment of the documentary describing a BCI 'opt-out' program that no historical record confirms ever existed — suggesting it was inserted as disinformation.
One of the documentary's original interview subjects, now very old, wants to publicly retract their testimony but lacks the legal standing to do so under Vantablack's content ownership statutes.
The annotated Unclocked version contains one annotation that wasn't added by the Collective — someone else got there first.
